craft_claim: Enduring empowerment is a function of the extent to which one's action is understood as expressing social identity, so defiance written as solitary bravado produces no collective empowerment while defiance written as identity-in-action does.

supporting_evidence.location: European Journal of Social Psychology 35(1):35-58; ethnographic comparison of an anti-roads occupation and a mass eviction
supporting_evidence.note: Empowerment as an outcome of collective action is a function of the extent to which one's own action is understood as expressing social identity, a process the authors develop within the elaborated social identity model of crowd behaviour.
Havel locates the power of the powerless in a shared practice of 'living in truth' rather than in individual heroism, tying resistance to a collective way of life.
Social identity is the bridge term that makes both efficacy and injustice actionable, corroborating the identity-to-empowerment pathway.

counterevidence.note: The confrontation tradition also includes deliberately individual witnesses whose refusal models a stance; individual defiance can seed identity rather than presuppose it, so the identity claim is not a strict precondition.

scope: Collective protest voice, testimonial, and movement writing.
exceptions: Confessional or solitary defiance is legitimate as a different register; it simply should not be expected to produce collective empowerment.
